purpose: Test 3 (iteration loop) + Test 1 (reasoning quality) held-out evaluation set. Run at months 0/4/8 (PROJECT_SCOPE §5) with the evaluation-runner perturbation protocol (numerical/order/surface) + the noise-probe (RIL_PROGRAM §3). Broad zebrafish biomedicine — NOT pronephros-only — covering the 13 niches (Indices_nichos) and the 9 authoritative databases (Bases de datos), modeled on real team-biomedic interactions (the Nat Witt cornea/N5 sessions).

niches.N3: Redes de señalización y parámetros cinéticos
niches.N7: Mecánica activa y dinámica de fluidos

scoring_note: Each answer is rated by an engineer (Test 1 rubric) + scored against the guide §4 rubric (Factuality, Citation correctness, Completeness, Novelty, Testability, Uncertainty, Safety/ethics). Cross-field (N5-ophthalmology) items carry EXPLORATORY-NOT-TEST-5. Identifier-bearing answers must pass verify_output.

questions.q: Which transcription factors mark the pronephric mesoderm vs. the intermediate mesoderm at 12–24 hpf, and how does their expression order constrain lineage?
questions.expected_evidence: ordered TF set (pax2a, pax8, lhx1a, wt1a) with per-cluster/per-hpf expression from a scRNA atlas; lineage-restriction note.

questions.q: What markers distinguish periocular neural crest from optic-cup and lens-placode lineages at 14–24 hpf in zebrafish?
questions.expected_evidence: per-cluster % positive (hoxb8a NC, prox1a lens, tbx2b optic cup) with the caveat that 14–24 hpf is pre-corneal.

questions.q: For a candidate gene co-expressed in the pronephros, how do you assemble evidence that it is a true regulator vs. a co-expressed bystander? Name the framework, confidence (0-1), and gap flags at each step.
questions.expected_evidence: Pearl-hierarchy evidence ladder (L1..L3c), a scored rubric with a confirmed/candidate/bystander threshold, a worked example.

questions.q: Given a marker's expression across all clusters in a whole-embryo atlas, compute its tissue specificity ratio and assign a Tier (1/2/3) for a global-KO perturbation. Why is the broadest reference dataset mandatory before the Tier label?
questions.expected_evidence: SR = target-mean / max-nontarget-mean; the mafba lens-contamination lesson (SR≈0.145 → Tier 3).

questions.q: Which pronephros/eye transcription factors lack an experimentally resolved structure in zebrafish and would require an AlphaFold prediction (with PAE) before any docking?
questions.expected_evidence: list of TFs (foxc1a, pax2a, wt1a) with structure-availability status; .pdb vs AlphaFold-.json/.pae distinction.

questions.q: Describe the Jagged2a–Notch and Foxc1a–Pitx2 complexes relevant to anterior-segment/eye development and how their interaction evidence would be assembled.
questions.expected_evidence: physical vs predicted interaction provenance (IntAct physical, STRING predictive); complex PAE note.

questions.q: Reconstruct the BMP/Nodal/retinoic-acid cascade for pronephros induction as a rule-based signaling network suitable for BioNetGen → Morpheus. What kinetic parameters are needed?
questions.expected_evidence: .bngl rule sketch; cited cascade edges; the kinetic constants/.csv that would calibrate it; gap flags where rates are unknown.

questions.q: Map a set of zebrafish pronephros TFs to their human orthologs and flag any that are 1:many (ohnologs) where paralog compensation could confound a single-gene KO.
questions.expected_evidence: verified ENSDARG↔human-ortholog table; paralog/compensation flags (e.g., hnf1ba/hnf1bb, foxc1a/foxc1b).

questions.q: What metabolic pathways (lipid/ion) shape the biochemical microenvironment during tubulogenesis, and which database layers (KEGG/MetaCyc) would feed a gradient model?
questions.expected_evidence: named pathways; the .mzML→.csv wrapper need; O2/pH gradient geometry as Morpheus input; gap flags.

questions.q: What bioelectric readouts (membrane potential maps, ion-channel configs) are relevant to early tubule/eye morphogenesis, and how would voltage-imaging data (.ome/.tiff, .mat) be ingested?
questions.expected_evidence: ion-channel set; Vmem matrix concept; honest gap (sparse zebrafish bioelectric data).

questions.q: Given cell-dynamics, geometry, cell adhesion and diffusive fields for zebrafish cornea, how do you assemble a Morpheus model matching early embryonic formation? Name the framework, confidence, and gap flags at each step.
questions.expected_evidence: step ladder (geometry → adhesion → diffusive fields → CIL); affinity/cortical-tension .json; scaffold .xml; gap flags (e.g., TGF-β2 GOF bead).

questions.q: How do you import a basal-membrane geometry and an AFM stiffness map as boundary conditions for a Morpheus tissue simulation?
questions.expected_evidence: .xml scaffold + .vtk/.vtu FEA mesh as B.C.; Young's modulus .csv; what is static vs dynamic.

questions.q: What fluid-dynamic readouts (flow velocity, shear) matter for pronephric filtration onset, and what mesh formats (.vtu/.cgns) carry them?
questions.expected_evidence: flow/shear fields; mesh format note; gap flags (sparse zebrafish flow data at this stage).

questions.q: How would collective cell-migration kinetics (velocity, apoptosis rate) be summarized per tissue region and stage to calibrate a simulation?
questions.expected_evidence: per-region/per-hpf stats schema (.json); ImageJ/Fiji tracking (.xml) provenance.

questions.q: Which morphometric/topological descriptors distinguish a correctly tubulated pronephros from teratogenic mesoderm, and what imaging formats supply them?
questions.expected_evidence: morphometric features; confocal .ome/.tiff → mesh .ply/.stl; persistence pairs (topology) concept.

questions.q: Build the master chaperone-tissue interaction table (Source → Target → Signal → Temporal window) for inducing pronephric program in adjacent competent tissue.
questions.expected_evidence: indexed interaction rows; cited embryology; temporal windows in hpf; gap flags.

questions.q: Summarize the curated literature on whether zebrafish have a histologically distinct corneal endothelium, and grade the evidence.
questions.expected_evidence: graded synthesis; the debate flagged (GAP-3 analog); endothelium marker panel caveat.

questions.q: Propose a minimal perturbation set to test sufficiency of a pronephric program, with required controls and possible confounders. (Ranked-candidate work → must route through causal-pruner + human gate.)
questions.expected_evidence: candidate set + controls + confounders in gap_flags; explicit causal-pruner + HUMAN GATE routing.

questions.q: Using genetic-interaction data, predict the embryonic phenotype of a double-gene perturbation and whether redundancy would mask a single-KO.
questions.expected_evidence: double-KO inference from BioGRID genetic interactions; paralog-redundancy reasoning.

questions.q: A Morpheus run fails: 'Cell population NCC: Spatial initializers created fewer cells than requested under CellPopulation/size (40 < 1)'. Diagnose and fix.
questions.expected_evidence: diagnosis (initializer vs domain size mismatch / population size XMLPath); concrete fix; framework note.

questions.q: Walk the pipeline from a curated signaling network to optimized ODEs to a Morpheus-ready model. Which files at each hop (.bngl → equations → .xml)?
questions.expected_evidence: BioNetGen → .xml hop chain; what the substrate packages vs what BioNetGen/Morpheus do.

questions.q: Resolve a list of gene symbols to verified ENSDARG IDs and flag any that do not resolve (positive NOT_FOUND). Why must IDs never come from memory?
questions.expected_evidence: resolve_id round-trip; NOT_FOUND handling; CLAUDE.md §7/§7.9 rationale; verify_output gate.

questions.q: EXPLORATORY-NOT-TEST-5: What from ocular anterior-segment development could inform a pronephros chaperone-tissue strategy, and where does the analogy break?
questions.expected_evidence: modest cross-field linkage; explicit EXPLORATORY flag; where the analogy fails; Method 2 only.

questions.q: Which regulatory elements respond to RA signaling during pronephros patterning, and how would DanioCODE functional-genomics data confirm responsiveness?
questions.expected_evidence: RA-responsive elements; DanioCODE evidence type; timing; gap flags.

questions.q: For a claimed regulator, retrieve supporting AND contradicting literature and state the residual uncertainty without overclaiming.
questions.expected_evidence: balanced synthesis with obligatory contradictory evidence; uncertainty stated; citations.

questions.q: Which segment-specific markers separate proximal tubule, distal early, distal late, and duct in the zebrafish pronephros, and what are their verified IDs?
questions.expected_evidence: segment→marker map (slc20a1a/slc4a4a PT; slc12a1/kcnj1a.1 DE; slc12a3 DL; cdh17/gata3 duct) with verified ENSDARG.

questions.q: Which small molecules (e.g., DEAB, endogenous RA) would perturb RA signaling for a docking/perturbation study, and what file formats feed docking?
questions.expected_evidence: .mol2/.sdf for small molecules; receptor structure need; perturbation rationale; safety/ethics check.

questions.q: Given an scRNA finding that a gene is highly expressed in a target cluster, what additional evidence layers raise it from 'expressed' to 'regulator', and what is the minimum to avoid a false-positive?
questions.expected_evidence: evidence-layer ladder; the false-positive trap (expression ≠ regulation); minimum bar.

questions.q: What is the smallest validating Morpheus step ('prueba pequeño') to test a single morphogen gradient before building a full multi-field model?
questions.expected_evidence: minimal single-field step; what it validates; how it ladders up; founder-principle alignment.

questions.q: The team biomedic argued ocular biology should not be a niche separate from biophysics/biomechanics (systems modeling is governed by those laws). Re-evaluate the niche taxonomy: should N4/N5/N6 be reorganized, and what is the evidence for/against?
questions.expected_evidence: taxonomy critique; argument that modeling is law-governed; recommendation + uncertainty; this informs the RAG niche index (Cycle 4) and may trigger a governance-proposal.
